The Los Angeles Chargers. A professional football franchise that relocated to Los Angeles in 2017 after 56 years in San Diego.

Born from the divisive relocation of the storied San Diego Chargers, they share a stadium with the Los Angeles Rams and compete in the AFC West. Despite early promise and star quarterback Philip Rivers, the franchise has struggled to establish identity or success in Los Angeles, never reaching the Super Bowl and facing persistent questions about fan loyalty in their new market.

The Chargers relocated from San Diego to Los Angeles in 2017 following contentious negotiations with the city, taking many fans and decades of franchise history with them. They played one season in 2017 at the StubHub Center, later called Dignity Health Sports Park, before moving to SoFi Stadium in 2020, sharing the facility with the Los Angeles Rams.

Philip Rivers continued as quarterback through 2019 after the relocation, maintaining individual excellence but failing to restore the playoff success the franchise had sought. The team never reached a Super Bowl as the Los Angeles franchise, despite high preseason expectations, becoming a symbol of relocation's disruptive effect on organizational momentum.

The Chargers drafted star pass rusher Joey Bosa in 2016 and developed promising young talent, but inconsistent management decisions and coaching changes hampered sustained success. They struggled with fan support in Los Angeles, where sports culture remains divided among established franchises like the Lakers and Dodgers, and where NFL fan populations remain less densely concentrated than in San Diego.

The relocation decision generated significant controversy. Team owner Dean Spanos overruled an NFL owners' vote and a San Diego ballot measure that opposed the move, representing a turning point in franchise-city relations.
